findings.reason: the census should call `transcript_index`/`session_usage`'s record filter so transcript parsing has one owner rather than two.
findings.text: §2 counts `storage-slow` tool results "from the transcripts" by walking `~/.claude/projects` itself, but that root is already owned at `reckon/velocity.py:1363` (`transcript_index`) and `reckon/velocity.py:1384` (`session_usage`), which already resolve the root, glob the `*.jsonl` session files, filter by window and skip sidechain records; a second walk forks the record-shape handling and drifts on the next transcript-schema change

findings.reason: the plan names the wrong file as the owner, so an implementation node would fork harness-home writes into a second module and collide with the idempotent seeding contract.
findings.text: §7 declares its write path as `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` ("which writes the run's harness home"), but the harness home is seeded by `_seed_harness_entry` in `reckon/_backends.py` (called at `reckon/_backends.py:2183`), and it skips any destination that already exists, so a settings writer added in dispatch.py is a second writer beside the owner; the project-MCP disabling belongs in the seeding path

findings.reason: naming `reckon/velocity.py` and `reckon/_backends.py` as the mechanisms most resembling the proposed additions would let the author extend rather than rebuild them.
findings.text: the plan searched for `_run_under_deadline` and the `doctor` MCP-config reader (it cites both), but cites no search over the transcript machinery (`reckon/velocity.py`) for §2's storage-slow count and none over the harness-home seeding for §7; a reader cannot tell whether the author looked and rejected those mechanisms or did not look

findings.reason: the section must account for its added surface in its own text, naming what it retires or why the retirement is impossible.
findings.text: §2 adds the `reckon doctor mcp` shape with `--since` and `--json` to the CLI-option family without naming anything §2 retires, merges, or a reason nothing can be

findings.reason: the section must name in its own text the surface it retires or merges, making the added dispatch option budget-accounted.
findings.text: §7 adds a `--mcp <name>` dispatch option, and while it retires the default (project servers enabled by default), it never states that the launch default it disables is the surface it retires, nor names any CLI option it removes

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3 and §8 extend the existing deep body-runner `_run_under_deadline` (reckon/mcp.py:299) and §2 concentrates the census in one new module rather than spreading it across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 re-reads Claude Code transcripts (owner `reckon/velocity.py`) and two sections write harness settings the owner `_seed_harness_entry` seeds.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1586, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 and §7 add CLI options without naming what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 adds a transcript-counting reader and §7 a harness-settings writer without citing the modules that already own those mechanisms.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §5 extends the existing `doctor` (reckon/cli.py:8455) rather than forking a second drift/launch reader, and §3 adds a field to the existing `TimeoutResult` (reckon/_mcp_tools.py:112) with a stated reason for keeping the `storage-slow` sentinel.
